title: Testing State
description: Learn how to test React components that use local state, Context, Redux, and React Query using React Testing Library and Vitest.

data.text: Testing stateful components does not require testing implementation details. The goal is to verify that the **user** sees the right thing at the right time. If a button toggles a menu, your test should check whether the menu is visible after the click — not whether a particular `useState` call happened inside the component.

React Testing Library encourages this user-centric approach. It renders your component into a real DOM, lets the user interact with it, and asserts on visible output. This philosophy applies equally well to components using useState, Context, Redux, or React Query.
For a component with local state, simulate the user actions that cause state changes and assert on the visible result. Do not reach into the component's internals.

data.title: Testing a Toggle Component

data.text: To test a component that consumes Context, wrap it in the provider just like your application does. Create a test wrapper that includes all providers the component needs. Do not mock the Context — use the real provider with test values.

data.title: Wrapper for Context-Dependent Components

data.text: React Query components depend on an asynchronous cache. Wrap them in a `QueryClientProvider` with a test query client. Mock the API calls using MSW (Mock Service Worker) or by mocking `fetch`. MSW is preferred because it intercepts requests at the network level and tests the full data flow.

data.title: Testing a Query Component with MSW
Testing Philosophy
data.text: Test what the user experiences: visible text, enabled or disabled buttons, error messages. Avoid testing internal state values or hook return objects directly. Tests that assert on implementation details break when you refactor, even when the user-facing behavior is unchanged.

data.title: Key Takeaways
items: Assert on user-visible output, not on useState internals
Wrap Context-dependent components in their real providers for tests
Use MSW to mock API responses for React Query tests
Tests should survive internal refactors; only break when behavior changes
